clips.speaker: Channing Frye
clips.text: When I got to Phoenix, Grant Hill was like, 'Listen, people are going to talk shit about you. But we're going to win.' He goes, 'Channing, Steve is a two-time MVP. Amar'e Stoudemire is like a four-time All-Star. You see Jason Richardson, he's like a two or three-time All-Star. You standing right here and doing your job and being available to shoot and working on that creates opportunities for everyone else to play four-on-four basketball.' So when I got to Cleveland, I was like, 'Shump, we know you're great. I respect the shit out of Shump. Shump is very talented. But Shump compared to talent compared to Kevin, Kyrie, Swish, and Bron, you got to simplify your game so that your consistency we can rely on.' And that was my attitude towards it. It's like, dude, look what Kevin is doing. We had arguments, is Kevin the best power forward versus Tim Duncan? Those are real arguments. And now Kevin is doing Channing Frye things to win. clips.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
clips.text: Outside of having the talent, the two most important things to winning the championship, being on a team to win the championship, is number one, it's health and number two is sacrificing. If you're not going to sacrifice, you're not going to win. I went to the NBA Finals five times, I won once. And the one time that I won is because everybody lost themselves in the team. Kevin Garnett set the tone from the jump, the first day of training camp in Rome. He came in and he said, 'Doc, before you get started, we're going to run this offense through Paul and Ray.' The world knew that Kevin Garnett was the best player on our team. No, we're going to run this offense. If you need me, I'm here, I'm going to focus defensively. That set the tone early.
clips.news_angle: Kevin Garnett set the tone for the 2008 Celtics championship
clips.social_post: Kendrick Perkins shares how Kevin Garnett set the tone for the 2008 Celtics: He told Doc Rivers to run the offense through Paul and Ray. The world knew KG was the best player, but he chose to focus on defense to win.
clips.video_title: Frustrated With His Cavs Role, Shump Was Told to Watch Kevin Love
clips.pull_quote: Kevin Garnett set the tone from the jump, the first day of training camp in Rome.

clips.speaker: Kendrick Perkins
clips.text: For a young guy like Shump that was like in his prime, coming off of ACL injury, has started off with the Knicks extremely well, was, you know, shit was looking promising, yeah you want to win a championship, but you want to get to a bag, you want to make a couple of All-Star games, you want to see where your talent actually is going to take you. So it's a real moment to highlight and show the world and show these teams out here that are actually trying to win right now this season, that it's one thing to talk about it and have the talent, but the hardest thing in the world is to sacrifice. You have to do an outstanding job of policing and keeping yourself accountable and making sure you sacrifice.
clips.news_angle: The difficulty of sacrificing individual goals for team championship success
clips.social_post: Kendrick Perkins on the reality of NBA winning: It is one thing to talk about it and have the talent, but the hardest thing in the world is to sacrifice. You have to do an outstanding job of policing and keeping yourself accountable.

clips.pull_quote: It's one thing to talk about it and have the talent, but the hardest thing is to sacrifice.

clips.text: Do you look at them as a top-tier contender, up there with San Antonio and maybe Houston in the Western Conference, or are you seeing some things that might make you want to bump them down a notch? You'll have Austin Reaves when he comes back being healthy, but I think sometimes when it comes down to it, it's like, you have to stop relying on the special stuff and you have to rely on what your identity is going to be.

clips.speaker: Chris Mannix
clips.text: Where I get concerned though is what I see the lapses I sometimes see on the defensive end. They are a very opportunistic defense. They are among the top five teams in steals, blocks, and I think number one in steals. They play the passing games extremely well. But defensive rating, they're in the bottom third of the NBA. They turn the ball over a lot, bottom 10 in the league in turnovers, and the bench doesn't produce all that much. Now some of that of course is Austin Reaves when he comes back, it will bump some production down to that bench. But they've got some warning signs there. Walker Kessler has been pretty healthy for most of the season, but he's been injured in the past, most recently most of last season. And if he goes out, he's just as irreplaceable to me as Luka Dončić. That sounds blasphemous, but who do they have that can step into that Walker Kessler role and give them rebounding, shot-blocking, clean up things on the defensive end?
